entries.title: Prescribed FPP path exponential shortcut bound (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For iid finite nonnegative nondegenerate edge weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, choose finite 0<=a<b with q=P(t<=a)>0 and p=P(t>=b)>0. Let integer L>=2 satisfy L(b-a)>2a, R=2(L+1), D=1+2R(R+1), eta=p^L q^(L+2). Every deterministic simple N-edge path gamma has P(gamma is a full-lattice geodesic) <= (1-eta)^ceil(floor(N/L)/D).
assumptions: Not a proof of the unrestricted no-bigeodesics conjecture; see the exact hypotheses in the statement.

entries.title: FPP geodesic exclusion from small deterministic dictionaries (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For iid finite nonnegative nondegenerate weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, choose finite 0<=a<b with q=P(t<=a)>0 and p=P(t>=b)>0, integer L>=2 with L(b-a)>2a, R=2(L+1), D=1+2R(R+1), and eta=p^L q^(L+2). For any deterministic finite dictionary P_N of simple N-edge paths, P(some member is a geodesic) <= |P_N|(1-eta)^ceil(floor(N/L)/D). Thus if these products tend to zero, almost surely there is no geodesic ray starting at a specified vertex whose N-edge prefix belongs to P_N for every N. In particular subexponential dictionary cardinality suffices. The result excludes bigeodesics only when one of their tails is covered by such dictionaries.
assumptions: Not a proof of the unrestricted no-bigeodesics conjecture; see the exact hypotheses in the statement.

entries.title: FPP square selection annihilates an iid shortcut pattern (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For iid Uniform[1,2] weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, the full-lattice geodesic between (0,0) and (1,1) is almost surely the cheaper of the two two-edge square routes A,B. For fixed A, the event both A edges >=7/4 and both B edges <=5/4 has probability 1/256. For the minimizing route R, the event both R edges >=7/4 and both other square-route edges <=5/4 is impossible, also conditional on R=A or R=B. A fixed-route iid shortcut probability therefore need not survive weight-dependent route selection.
assumptions: Not a proof of the unrestricted no-bigeodesics conjecture; see the exact hypotheses in the statement.

entries.title: Invalid iid shortcut transfer after path selection (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. REFUTED INFERENCE: a shortcut event with positive iid probability for each prescribed path retains that probability after selecting a minimizing path from the same edge weights. The Uniform[1,2] square example gives a fixed-route pattern probability 1/256 and selected-route probability zero. A derived conditional law, independent selection, or valid deterministic dictionary bound is required.
assumptions: Not a proof of the unrestricted no-bigeodesics conjecture; see the exact hypotheses in the statement.

relations.rationale: The dictionary statement applies the exact C05 bound to each prescribed member and uses a union bound; no cross-path independence is assumed.
The endpoints are exact: the inference demands retaining a positive shortcut-pattern probability; the actual selected-square pattern probability is zero.
